title: Chained cuts evaluate in the kernel again
summary: A part authored as a chain of differences — a plate, then a bore, then a hole, then another — no longer crashes the browser kernel into a mesh-only fallback.
details: The evaluator batches a chain of booleans into one cut against the union of the tools, and bounded that attempt with a wall-clock reading that does not exist in WebAssembly: taking it panicked, and the panic took the whole kernel module down. The web app hid this almost perfectly — it caught the crash and re-evaluated the document in TypeScript, so the part still appeared, just without its B-rep and without the kernel's speed, and the only trace was a line in the console. Anything that needs the real surfaces rather than a mesh found nothing there: sectioning a part for CAM would simply fail on a plate with a few holes in it. The batching budget is now taken from the clock the caller supplies (the browser's own `performance.now()`), and a caller that has none gets a deterministic cap on how many merges the batching may attempt, so it is bounded on every platform rather than on none. Both paths produce the same solid, and a source guard in the test suite stops the wall clock being reintroduced.
